eligibility.quote: I just updated my Groovy debian installation with the release that was posted today on ros-users and now collada meshes no longer appear in RViz.  In particular, the TurtleBot is now basically invisible.

loudness.quote: Actually, it doesn't look like scaling, but it is pretty messed up on my machine as well (whole robot is just a few speckles of gray and white scattered around)

resolution.quote: turtlebot_create version 2.0.1 fixes this issue. It's now available on shadow-fixed.

notes: Verified rviz#622 (+comments), turtlebot#65 (+comments) and the fix merge 9299530. Eligibility agreed at step 6 (UPGRADE; unit-aware rviz 1.9.28 renders meshes authored for unit-ignoring rviz). I confirmed in the fix diff that create_body.dae's declaration changes from <unit meter="0.01" name="centimeter"/> to <unit meter="1.0" name="meter"/> — a unit mismatch on the mesh resource, so unit_mismatch on resource:package://create_description/meshes/create_body.dae is right. Loudness disagreement: the spec records loud_documented/'connect' with the template sentence 'the consumer logs an incompatibility error naming the element before any data is exchanged', which describes nothing in this source. What rviz#622 and turtlebot#65 show is wrong rendering observed at run time — 'the TurtleBot is now basically invisible', 'whole robot is just a few speckles of gray and white scattered around' — with no diagnostic from tooling at build, connection, or activation; users diagnosed the scale factor by hand ('applying the following scales to the meshes fixed the problem: ... create_body: 100'). That is silent_documented with detection_stage run. Resolution recommended agreed: bit-pirate's '2.0.1 fixes this issue' is a release statement, not a shown observation of 2.0.1 rendering correctly against a named rviz revision; pirobot's working observation used his own rescaled mesh copies.
